items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: I play some of his licks... I phrase the way he would have phrased it... Roy Eldridge got his inspiration from Ray Allen and Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Now, the reason why I like this book, I've never heard Louis Armstrong play it. But I can always hear him with my mind's ear playing this. Because it sounds like he should have played this number. And if you notice, on my chorus, I play some of his licks. Not many of his exact licks. In other words, I play, I phrase the way he would have phrased it. On spots. Not all the way through my solo. But some spots on my solo I phrase it. Was he any good? Oh, Louis Armstrong? Yes, he did. He said the style, he said the…
You don't think he was just a clown?

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: That was the first time I heard Louis Armstrong was at the rhythm club. Louis Armstrong came and I had to play one Sunday.

ctx.x: mother's side. Yeah. Mm-hmm. Anyway, I have a lot more to ask you. Were there any saloons in your neighborhood? You said you played at different places, but would you play at places in your neighborhood?

No, no. There were saloons in the neighborhood, but they didn't have any music. Now, there was music downtown, and some of the places uptown, like the Pigpen. Did you go to the Pigpen? Oh, I went there once. Now those are the players who played, like the Pigpen and some of those old places, Louis Armstrong played there. See, a lot of people think that Louis Armstrong played on Bourbon Street. Because people come in and ask me, they say, oh, did Louis Armstrong play here? No. And when he played at Preservation…
with Fletcher Henderson. Well, you mentioned the Pigpen. Did you ever, that was on Decatur Street?
